pages.title: Sugars
pages.text: Sugars are indulgent foods that provide quick energy. $(#e05252)Penalty:$() reduced sprint speed when depleted. $(#52c252)Bonus:$() increased jump height when maintained. A little goes a long way — don't overdo it.

pages.title: Vanilla Sugar Sources
pages.text:
$(bold)Honey Bottle$() — best vanilla sugar; also clears poison. Renewable from bee farms.
$(bold)Honeycomb$() — counts as Sugars when eaten; byproduct of beekeeping.
$(bold)Cookie$() — overlaps with Grains; counts for both depending on config.
$(bold)Cake$() — each slice counts as Sugars; one cake covers multiple days.
$(bold)Pumpkin Pie$() — may count toward Sugars as well as Grains.

pages.title: Sugars — Honey
pages.text:
Honey bottles are an excellent sugar source that also clears poison. Keeping a bee farm gives you a steady supply of both honey bottles and honeycomb, covering this group with minimal effort.

A bee farm with 4–6 hives produces more than enough honey to keep Sugars maxed indefinitely.

pages.title: Be Careful with Excess
pages.text:
The Sugars group decays faster than others and is easier to overshoot. Eating too much sugar pushes the bar into the excess range above 80%, which $(#e05252)reduces nutrition absorption$() until it decays back down.

Eat sugar foods in small amounts regularly rather than binging a stack of cookies in one sitting.

pages.title: Bee Farm Setup
pages.text:
A basic bee farm needs only 3 bees per hive and flowers nearby. Bees fill their hive passively during the day. Use a $(bold)dispenser with shears$() or $(bold)dispenser with bottles$() to automate harvesting honey bottles and honeycomb.

Even a manual bee farm with 2–3 hives produces enough to never worry about Sugars again.

pages.title: Rotation Strategy
pages.text:
Honey and cake are different sugar families. Alternating between honey bottles and cake slices gives better nutrition than using only one source.

Sugars is the group most players neglect early on because vanilla sugar sources require more setup. Prioritize building a bee farm or sugar cane supply — once established, this group almost runs itself.
